title: Fewer billing support calls
demand: Support is drowning in billing calls since the new pricing. Let's add a chatbot so customers can answer their own invoice questions. We want lower support cost and we suspect confused customers churn more.
context: B2B web app, billing area; account admins are the ones who call

B.why: Outcome named (E-002) and support cost has a baseline (E-001); not higher because churn is only suspected.

U.why: Who calls is known, but not what they struggle with; not 0 because E-001 shows billing is the top call reason.

S.statement: Add a chatbot for billing questions.
S.why: Articulated, but nothing links a chatbot to the reason customers call.

hypotheses.statement: add a chatbot to answer billing questions
hypotheses.origin: head of support, in the intake demand
hypotheses.test: share of billing questions resolved without an agent

hypotheses.origin: head of support, in the intake demand
hypotheses.test: churn of accounts that called about billing vs those that did not

evidence.claim: Billing questions are the largest category of support calls in the last quarter.
evidence.limitations: call reasons are tagged by agents, not by customers

evidence.claim: Lowering support cost is the desired outcome.
evidence.source: intake with the head of support
evidence.limitations: a desired outcome is not evidence of a problem
